# 132. AI-rusning, elchock och en riktigt dålig julklapp

**Feed**: borssurr  
**Published**: 2026-11-20  
**Market Sentiment**: Negative

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

The hosts describe a rough week in the markets: equities, metals, oil and bitcoin all fell, fund managers cut tech exposure at the fastest pace in 20 years, and the Anthropic IPO was seen as a possible test of the AI trade. A big theme is surging Swedish electricity prices hurting consumers at the same time as rate hikes from the Fed and ECB, which one host fears could push towards a financial crisis. Company talk centred on Hemnet's collapse, Klarna's consumer-credit risk, the Handelsbanken A/B share gap, private equity selling to itself (Nordic Capital/Karo) and AI-driven cost cutting at Fortnox.

---

## Universe Stocks

### ⛔ HEM — Hemnet | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Down 33% in a week; guest says the Booli copy destroys the premium value of paid listings. Shorted by Alcur.

#### Reasoning

Guest Nika Mikides (a heavy Hemnet user) argues that years of price hikes let Booli in, and that scraping estate-agent listings now buries paid ads, so sellers no longer feel the premium is worth paying. The hosts call the price action terrible. The one upside case is that Sprints Capital may be pushing the price down ahead of a buyout.

#### Sell Triggers

- buyout bid from Sprints Capital
- restoration of the premium listing experience
- new CEO strategy that stabilises listing volumes

> *"Men idag så känner jag inte den här premiumkänslan som jag kände att jag ändå behövde betala förut."*

---

### ⛔ KLAR — Klarna | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Host and a Handelsbanken analyst are sceptical: buy-now-pay-later is the lowest-quality consumer credit, with US unemployment and Fed hikes ahead.

#### Reasoning

Handelsbanken analyst Martin Ekstedt (who does not cover the stock) thinks the US consumer-credit sector is not priced for a downturn, with earlier and larger losses in buy-now-pay-later. A host adds that Fed hikes and stressed lower-income consumers make it hard for consumer-credit firms. Research firm Trist sees value, but the hosts disagree.

#### Sell Triggers

- Fed stops hiking
- US credit losses stay low
- US labour market stays strong

> *"Jag är skeptisk. Jag tror de här konsumentkreditbolagen får det väldigt svårt."*

---

### 🟢 SHB-B — Handelsbanken | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Big A/B price gap; advice is to own the cheapest share class, since dividends are what count.

#### Reasoning

The hosts note the large premium on the scarcer share class, possibly driven by passive index flows. Because both classes get the same dividend, the cheaper class gives more yield per krona. Nordic banks are also described as doing very well with good macro, though highly valued on historical multiples.

#### Sell Triggers

- A/B gap closes
- Nordic bank credit quality worsens

> *"Köp den billigaste, för det är utdelning som är det viktiga i spelet här."*

---

### 🟠 RVRC — Revolution Race | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 40%

Strong report on Thursday; outdoor trend and the I Can I Will brand acquisition look promising, but consumer confidence risks from power prices loom.

#### Reasoning

The hosts congratulate RVRC on a fine report and point to the outdoor trend and its newly bought brand. They also warn that rising electricity prices, rate hikes and market stress could weaken retail just as it was recovering.

#### Sell Triggers

- consumer confidence falls on electricity prices
- weak Christmas trading

> *"Vi var inne på Revolution Race. Grattis till dem, bra rapport."*

---
